feedback.Isolate Host: CRITICAL CONTAINMENT SUCCESS: WS-ENG-SENIOR02 isolated immediately via EDR! Off-hours NetFlow volume telemetry (4.2 GB egress) combined with the rclone process execution confirmed an unauthorized insider exfiltration event. Host isolation severed the transfer before the full intellectual property archive could be stolen.
feedback.Block IP: PARTIAL MITIGATION: Blocked external Wasabi IP at perimeter firewall. However, the insider retained active host control on the workstation and can re-route the transfer to personal Google Drive, Dropbox, or a USB mass storage device without endpoint network isolation.
feedback.Escalate: ACCEPTABLE: Escalated to Tier 2 SOC and HR/Legal Incident Response. In massive active data egress, isolating the host immediately stops file loss, but escalation ensures digital forensics preserves chain of custody.
feedback.Dismiss: CATASTROPHIC BREACH: Dismissed as regular remote work! Disgruntled engineer successfully exfiltrated the entire company proprietary software codebase to a competitor.

educational_rationale.topic: User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA), NetFlow Baselines & Insider Threat Detection
educational_rationale.certification_relevance: Security+ SY0-701 (Section 2.3 Threat Actors - Insiders, Section 4.2 Incident Response Analysis) & Network+ (Section 5.3 NetFlow & Traffic Flow Monitoring)
educational_rationale.deep_dive: Insider threats are challenging because the perpetrator possesses legitimate domain credentials and authorized access to files. Traditional signature AV will not trigger on file reads. Detection relies on User & Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) and NetFlow baseline deviation: (1) Temporal Anomaly: VPN connection and gigabyte-scale transfers occurring at 03:15 AM outside standard shift hours; (2) Volume Anomaly: Standard daily workstation egress is under 50 MB, but NetFlow logs 4.2 GB in 12 minutes; (3) Tooling Anomaly: Execution of cloud sync binaries like 'rclone' from user Temp directories directed toward unapproved cloud storage providers.
